integrity: The proof is self-contained apart from the classical analytic Gabriel theorem. It derives a regularized Laplacian comparison from the singular values of the harmonic differential, obtains H^1 control of both analytic components from the h^1 norm of f, and then applies Gabriel separately to the components. Zeros are handled by epsilon-regularization; no numerical experiment is used.
scientific_limitations: The result treats the endpoint p=1 for sense-preserving harmonic K-quasiregular maps in the disk. The explicit factor 4(K^2+1) is not claimed sharp, the case 0<p<1 is not resolved, and no theorem is claimed for general nonharmonic quasiregular Hardy classes without additional boundary hypotheses.
title: Quasiregularity restores Gabriel's convex-curve inequality at the endpoint
